item.title: Lee's approval rating falls back below 40%: poll
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating slipped back to 39 percent this week, a weekly poll showed Friday, amid negative sentiment over his real estate policies and economic concerns. The survey, conducted by Gallup Korea from Tuesday through Thursday on 1,002 people aged 18 and older, showed that positive assessments of Lee's performance fell 2 percentage points from the previous week, when the figure stood at 41 percent. Lee's approval rating has fluctuated around the 40 percent mark in recent weeks after hitting a low of 37 percent in October. Those who disapproved of Lee's handling of state affairs remained unchanged from the previous week at 50 percent. Real estate policies were cited the most by those who disapproved of Lee's performance at 17 percent, followed by economic and livelihood concerns at 15 percent. Among those who positively assessed Lee's performance, 19 percent cited economic and livelihood issues, followed by diplomacy at 17 percent and communication at 9 percent. The latest survey came amid political disputes over a controversial special counsel bill over allegatio

item.title: FM Cho heads to China for talks with Wang Yi on bilateral ties, prospects for NK-US dialogue
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun departed for China on Friday for talks with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on bilateral relations and issues concerning the Korean Peninsula, including the possibility of renewed dialogue between Washington and Pyongyang. Cho was scheduled to hold talks with Wang later in the day, followed by a dinner hosted by the Chinese foreign minister, according to the foreign ministry. "We plan to discuss the overall state of bilateral relations, particularly issues that need to be coordinated between the two countries ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit," Cho told reporters at Gimpo International Airport before departing for China. His visit comes ahead of President Lee Jae Myung's planned trip to China for the APEC summit in Shenzhen from Wednesday to Thursday, and the ministerial meeting was expected to help lay the groundwork for a potential meeting between Lee and Chinese President Xi Jinping. item.title: Winter blooms transform Seoul Botanic Park into festive garden
item.description: Tucked inside western Seoul’s Gangseo District, Seoul Botanic Park is defying the winter chill with a vibrant seasonal showcase of more than 40 tropical orchid varieties, 300 poinsettias and imaginative plant displays designed to liven up indoor spaces. The exhibition, titled “Between Winter and Plants,” runs from Friday through Jan. 31, 2027, across the park’s greenhouse, Seed Library and Garden Support Center. At the Tropical Hall, a display titled “Today, Orchids” features Aria, a miniature Phalaenopsis orchid developed domestically in 2019, alongside more than 40 varieties of tropical orchids, including Oncidium, Cattleya, Vanda and Cymbidium. The Mediterranean Hall presents a Christmas garden featuring 300 plants from 15 domestically developed poinsettia varieties, including red Flame, Green Star, peach Grace and Pink Bell. The display also features unusual spherical-bracted varieties called Sugar Ball, Red Ball and Snow Ball, while a fountain installation inspired by Rome incorporates a Christmas tree arrangement made with Flame poinsettias. item.title: N. Korea changes national flag's aspect ratio for 1st time since 1948
item.description: North Korea has revised its constitution to change its national flag's aspect ratio for the first time since its regime was established in 1948, according to the amended basic law posted on the website of Pyongyang's propaganda outlet. Article 166 of the revised constitution posted on Naenara's website stipulates that the ratio of the flag's height to its width is 1 to 1.65, replacing the previous ratio of 1 to 2. The change came as North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has sought to build his own governing style and national identity while retaining some legacies of his predecessors. The flag's 1-to-2 ratio rule had remained unchanged in the law until the North's constitutional revision in September 2023. Despite the ratio change, the overall design of the North's flag remains intact, consisting of a broad red stripe in the center, narrow white stripes above and below it, blue stripes above and below the white stripes, and a red five-pointed star in a white circle. item.title: Seoul files criminal complaints against 5 serial 119 prank callers
item.description: For the emergency dispatchers staffing Seoul’s 119 hotline — Korea’s equivalent of 911 — every second counts. Yet over the past year, a handful of individuals treated the city’s critical lifeline for fires, accidents, and medical emergencies as a personal bulletin board, a late-night cab service and a sounding board for drunken rants. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Friday that it had filed criminal complaints against five habitual callers who collectively flooded the 119 emergency dispatch center with 8,710 non-emergency calls and text messages between September 2025 and August 2026. The barrage intensified over the summer. Between June and August alone, the five individuals accounted for 4,034 separate contacts — an average of more than 40 disruptions a day. Among the worst offenders, one individual placed 2,661 phone calls, while another sent 2,886 text messages. According to the Seoul Emergency Operations Center, the nature of the contacts ranged from perplexing to blatantly disruptive. item.title: Korean economy continues to 'grow at solid pace': finance ministry
item.description: The Korean economy continues to "grow at a solid pace," although inflationary pressures stemming from high oil prices could weigh on people's livelihoods, the finance ministry said Friday. The Ministry of Finance and Economy offered the assessment in the November edition of its economic report, known as the Green Book, signaling a more positive view of economic conditions after previously describing the economy as continuing to "recover." The finance ministry began using the term "recovery" in November 2025 and maintained the assessment through October this year, except in April. In its April report, the ministry temporarily dropped the reference to "recovery," instead citing "increased downside risks" amid the Middle East war, before returning to the previous wording in May. "Recently, the Korean economy has continued to grow at a solid pace, supported by a substantial increase in exports and accelerating investment growth, with consumption improving gradually," the finance ministry said. item.title: Lee to hold bilateral talks with Thai, Philippine leaders at ASEAN summit
item.description: Korean President Lee Jae Myung will hold bilateral meetings with his Thai and Philippine counterparts next week on the sidelines of a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), his spokesperson said Friday. Presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung announced Lee's planned meetings as the Korean president is scheduled to attend the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in China. Lee will attend the ASEAN summit in Manila on Monday and Tuesday before traveling to China's Shenzhen on Wednesday for a two-day trip to attend the APEC summit. Lee will separately meet with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. on Monday afternoon on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit, Kang said in a press release. On the sidelines of the APEC summit Wednesday, Lee will hold a luncheon meeting with Korean residents in southern China, home to some 24,000 Korean nationals, she said.

On the sidelines of the APEC summit Wednesday, Lee will hold a luncheon meeting with Korean residents in southern China, home to some 24,000 Korean nationals, she said.

item.title: China's access to Nvidia chips in doubt as curbs gain traction in US Congress
item.description: US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government. Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development. And senior White House officials were discussing whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation said, as the desire to take action rose across Washington. A growing number of lawmakers have criticized Lutnick for the administration's refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist, and over whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia's exports to China. Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI

item.title: Gov't holds first task force meeting to ease living costs for wage earners
item.description: Korea on Friday held the inaugural meeting of a new task force aimed at developing policies to reduce living costs and boost real disposable income for wage earners. First Vice Finance Minister Kwon Dae-young chaired the meeting with officials from relevant ministries to discuss detailed implementation plans following the presidential office's announcement of the initiative this week. The task force comprises four working groups covering existing support measures, taxation, fiscal policy and finance, respectively, to identify practical ways to achieve those goals. The new team will focus particularly on helping workers cope with labor market changes driven by structural changes in industry, along with the growing financial burden of caring for children and elderly parents. Other key goals will include helping workers build assets, improve job security and manage their health. "The measures in the 2026 tax revision bill and next year's budget proposal are directly linked to wage earners' household finances next year," Kwon said. item.title: Seoul shares drop nearly 1%, erasing earlier gains following Nvidia jitters
item.description: Korean stocks fell almost 1 percent Friday as investors turned cautious over the potential impact of the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem. The local currency was trading lower against the U.S. dollar. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) closed down 52.20 points, or 0.98 percent, at 5,290.53. The index opened 2.05 percent higher and rose as high as 5,504.44 before shifting to negative territory around 12:35 p.m. Trade volume was light at 237.3 million shares worth 16 trillion won ($11.9 billion), with gainers edging decliners 450 to 418. Foreigners sold a net 550.5 billion won worth of stocks, while institutions bought 2.3 billion won and individuals purchased a net 17.2 billion won. Overnight on Wall Street, major stock indices closed lower following the exit of Huang, who played a crucial role in the recent AI boom. Investors were also awaiting the release of U.S. producer price data, which could give a clue to the Federal Reserve's monetary policy, following the steeper-than-expected rise in the consumer price index ea

item.title: Microsoft outage drags on for hours, disrupting Outlook, Teams for businesses and governments
item.description: Microsoft services such as Outlook and Teams were disrupted for about 10 hours on Thursday as the tech giant struggled to fix issues with some servers, hitting businesses and government agencies globally that use the popular platforms. In its latest update, Microsoft said efforts to improve serviceability were not progressing as expected. "We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances," it said. Downdetector, which tracks outages by collating status reports from a number of sources, showed more than 25,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US at 9:30 p.m. ET (0230 GMT). It also showed outages for several Microsoft services in the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia and Japan, early Friday local time. At its peak, Downdetector showed more than 130,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US around 1 p.m. ET on Thursday. item.title: Climate change made Indonesian fires more severe, scientists say
item.description: SINGAPORE — Wildfires that hit large parts of Indonesia from August to October and plunged much of Southeast Asia into hazardous smoke were made much worse by "record-breaking" heat caused by human-induced climate change, scientists said on Friday. While a very strong El Niño was the dominant factor in determining the extremely low levels of rainfall across Indonesia from July, human-induced climate change contributed around 1.6 degrees Celsius of additional heat during the fire season, said a report by climate research group World Weather Attribution. "The conditions that we saw this year would simply just not have happened in a world without the human contribution to climate change, even with the very strong El Niño that we're seeing," said Theodore Keeping, a researcher into wildfires and extreme weather at Imperial College London who contributed to the report. "You have multiple different drivers changing in different ways, but what we can say with very high confidence is that the driving weather conditions of these fires are getting more severe," he told a briefing. item.title: FBI says US has seized $1.2 bil. worth of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance
item.description: WASHINGTON — The FBI said Thursday that it had seized more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance , the world's largest crypto exchange. The theft of about $6.3 billion from Binance is regarded as the biggest crypto heist in history, and the FBI has previously attributed it to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor. The U.S. government and private sector have so far combined to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds, and the Justice Department said Thursday that it has now obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of that total. Typically in those situations, the U.S. government will file a claim of forfeiture with a judge, who will then determine who has a legitimate claim to the recovered funds. Also Thursday, the FBI blamed North Korea for a separate social engineering scheme that officials say resulted in the theft of $400 million worth of cryptocurrency over the last 18 months. item.title: ICE reports record-high immigration arrests and deportations since Trump's return to White House
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS — Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested and deported more people during the last fiscal year than at any time in its 23-year history, Homeland Security said Thursday, as President Donald Trump followed through on promises of mass deportations that helped him win back the White House in 2024 but also fueled the political blowback that led to Democrats’ overwhelming victory in last week’s midterm elections. The numbers released Thursday by the department reflect the massive funding that has gone into supercharging immigration enforcement under the Trump administration, with more money for deportation officers, detention facilities and deportation flights. But Democratic members of Congress, buoyed by their sweeping victories in both the House and Senate, are promising vigorous oversight of the agency core to the president's mass deportation mission. ICE said it deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30. item.title: Import prices fall again in October on stronger Korean won, lower oil prices
item.description: Import prices fell again in October driven by a stronger Korean won and lower oil prices, central bank data showed Friday. The import price index dropped 1.8 percent month-on-month last month, reversing from a 1.9 percent gain in September, according to the preliminary data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The index had declined for three consecutive months since June. The BOK said the month-on-month decline came as the Korean won strengthened against the U.S. dollar by 1.6 percent over the one-month period, while the price of Dubai crude, Korea's benchmark, fell 2.6 percent. Prices of raw materials decreased 3 percent in October from a month earlier, while intermediate goods dropped 1 percent over the cited period, according to the BOK data. Import prices are a key driver of inflation, as they affect production costs and consumer prices throughout the supply chain, according to the central bank. item.title: Korea, France hold joint coordinating committee on nuclear energy in Saclay
item.description: Korea and France commenced their 27th joint coordinating committee on nuclear energy in France's southwestern region of Saclay this week and discussed nuclear technology cooperation, Seoul's science ministry said Friday. The two-day event ending Friday (local time) comes as the two nations mark their 140th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year, the Ministry of Science and ICT added. The event has been organized since 1982, following the signing of a bilateral agreement on the peaceful use of nuclear energy in 1981. During the meeting, Korea and France discussed 21 areas of technological cooperation in fields such as nuclear energy research, nuclear safety and the nuclear industry. The two countries agreed to expand cooperation in next-generation nuclear reactors, as well as in the nuclear energy supply chain, following related memorandums of understanding signed during two bilateral summits this year, held in April and September. item.title: Binance says all asset losses from N. Korea-linked cyberattack covered
item.description: WASHINGTON — Global cryptocurrency exchange Binance said Thursday it has completed covering assets affected by a massive cyberattack blamed on North Korea, after committing more than $6.34 billion in company funds to make up for the losses. "Binance has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident," the company said in a statement posted on its website. The company said it used funds from its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), futures insurance fund and corporate treasury to cover the losses, while acquiring affected cryptocurrencies through market and over-the-counter transactions. "Binance has committed to replenishing SAFU to return the fund to approximately $1 billion, ensuring it remains fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve," it said. The announcement follows an Oct. 29 cyberattack in which hackers allegedly linked to North Korea stole more than $6 billion in digital assets from Binance. item.title: US House passes bill to protect small businesses from foreign adversaries, including N. Korea
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. House of Representatives has passed a bill aimed at protecting American small businesses from economic and cybersecurity threats posed by foreign adversaries, including North Korea. The House passed the Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026 on Wednesday, The bill would require the Small Business Administration (SBA) to provide small businesses with information and guidance on identifying and responding to threats from foreign adversaries. "China, Russia and North Korea are working to undermine our economic and national security, and American businesses are increasingly caught in the crosshairs," Rep. Roger Williams (R-TX) said during a House floor debate on Wednesday. The legislation seeks to help businesses address risks such as intellectual property theft, cyberattacks, counterfeit goods and predatory investment practices. It now subject to deliberation by the Senate. item.title: [WEEKENDER] Samsung Guide Dog School marks 33 years of changing lives
item.description: Samsung Guide Dog School, which marks its 33rd anniversary this year, is Korea’s first guide dog training institution and the world’s only guide dog school operated by a single corporation, with its operations fully funded by Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance. The school was established in September 1993 by late Samsung Group Chairman Lee Kun-hee as part of efforts to foster greater understanding and acceptance of people with disabilities. At the time, corporate involvement in guide dog training was unprecedented worldwide. The school became a full member of the International Guide Dog Federation in 1999 and went on to host the organization's general assembly in Korea in 2002. Lee was also honored by the federation that year for his efforts to raise awareness of people with disabilities. Since its first guide dog, Bada, was paired with a visually impaired person in 1994, the school has provided more than 320 guide dogs to visually impaired partners free of charge. Its responsibilities extend beyond raising and training guide dogs. The school also teaches visually impaired partners how

item.title: [WEEKENDER] How guide dogs and humans become partners
item.description: Completing professional training does not mean a guide dog is immediately ready to accompany a visually impaired person. The dog must first be matched with a suitable partner, and the two must learn to walk and live together. Few understand this process better than Yoo Seok-jong of Samsung Guide Dog School. Born with a visual impairment, Yoo now lives with his fifth guide dog. Drawing on his own experience, he helps visually impaired people find dogs suited to their needs and lifestyles. During an interview at the school in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, on Nov. 2, Yoo was accompanied by Gori, a 5-year-old demonstration dog. Yoo's own guide dog was at a veterinary clinic after falling ill that morning. Friendly and sociable, Gori normally helps introduce visitors to guide dogs and accompanies visually impaired people on trial walks. Yoo said one of the most important factors in matching a guide dog with a prospective partner is walking speed. "The person's walking speed needs to match the dog's natural pace," he said. item.title: [WEEKENDER] A day with Jerry, guide dog in training
item.description: As Jerry, a Labrador retriever, approached a crosswalk, he came to a stop at the curb. His trainer, Keum Jung-hun, had given no command. Jerry simply recognized the boundary between the sidewalk and the road and stopped on his own. Keum pressed a small device, producing a sharp click. Known as a clicker, the tool signals that Jerry has performed a task correctly. "It means he did a good job," Keum explained. "Verbal praise takes time, but a clicker lets us mark the exact moment he does something right." Jerry is an almost 2-year old guide dog in training. The Korea Times met him during a training session at Samsung Guide Dog School on Nov. 2. The school in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, is fully funded by Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance. After six to seven months of professional training, he has passed his final walking assessment and is now completing the remaining steps before being paired with a visually impaired partner. item.title: China's memory makers are catching up. What happens when they do?
item.description: The memory business has rarely had it this good, thanks to the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Korea’s chipmakers are reporting extraordinary earnings and unusual confidence that the good times will last. SK hynix’s third-quarter operating profit rose more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won ($62 billion), an operating margin of almost 80 percent. Samsung Electronics’ rose nearly ninefold to 107.4 trillion won, with its memory business setting records of its own. Across the West Sea, China’s challengers are sharing in the windfall. ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) remains far smaller, but its quarterly revenue rose more than sevenfold to 118.7 billion yuan ($17.8 billion), with a net profit attributable to shareholders of 54.4 billion yuan, reversing years of losses. CXMT and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) are the twin pillars of China’s drive for memory self-sufficiency, part of Beijing’s broader pursuit of technological independence facing U.S. export restrictions. item.title: Trump says US does not need Iran deal, directs Vance to focus on domestic corruption
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus "his complete and total attention" on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states. Trump's directive came a day after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vance was considering face-to-face peace talks with a hard-line Iranian security official and a week after the vice president blamed the costly war with Iran for Republicans' midterm elections drubbing. "We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!" Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Strait of Hormuz. item.title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had a relationship with a second employee, sources say
item.description: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful. Nvidia declined to comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia's board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name. item.title: 'I'd rather stay an intern': Why some Gen Z workers in Korea are choosing less responsibility
item.description: For some young Korean workers, leaving the office on time matters more than finishing every task, and avoiding the responsibilities of a permanent position can be more appealing than climbing the corporate ladder. These attitudes are emerging among members of Generation Z, who are challenging workplace expectations long shaped by loyalty, overtime and deference to senior colleagues. In a roundtable discussion organized by the Hankook Ilbo, young participants shared their views on work, career advancement and workplace relationships, revealing both generational differences and contradictions in their own approaches to professional life. Their experiences suggest that while younger employees increasingly demand clearer boundaries and more explicit instructions, they sometimes struggle to meet those same expectations when they become responsible for guiding others. Leaving work on time, even with tasks unfinished For Korea's Generation X, now largely in their 50s, staying late at the office was once considered a badge of dedication. item.title: Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's interim CEO?
item.description: CHICAGO — With Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, Nvidia is bringing longtime tech executive Colette Kress into the role of interim CEO. Kress first joined the California-based chipmaker back in 2013. She’s served as Nvidia's executive vice president and CFO ever since — and will now be stepping into the top post amid the company's most tumultuous chapter yet. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia over three decades ago and has since become a singular figure in the tech world, resigned after reports of his extramarital affairs came into the spotlight this week. He faced growing calls to step down after The New York Times reported on his relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy — and also late Wednesday, when the outlet and later others found Huang was said to have had another affair with an Nvidia employee. item.title: How a close friend of labor activist Jeon Tae-il keeps his legacy alive
item.description: Choi Jong-in, 78, still aches for his friend Jeon Tae-il, who was just 22. When Jeon set himself on fire in the middle of Pyeonghwa Market in Seoul's Jung District on Nov. 13, 1970, Choi was the first to rush to his side, taking off his jacket to smother the flames. “His hair was burning and curling like nylon fabric, his lips were turning inside out, but he sprang back to his feet and shouted, ‘We are not machines!” More than half a century has passed, and one might expect Choi to recount the incident with the composure of an elderly man who has come to terms with life. But for a while, he cannot bring himself to continue. He has never really given an interview about Jeon. While Jeon's mother, the late Lee So-sun (who died in 2011), was alive, Choi says he held back because he did not want to cause her further grief. Even after she passed away and was reunited with her son, he found it too painful to speak. The trauma never entirely left him, but it did not break him. item.title: Japanese Korean activist's takedown of far right goes viral online with 10 million views
item.description: In a 1996 debate program on Japan’s Asahi TV, right-wing commentators mocked former Korean comfort women for demanding an apology, sneering, “Isn’t all they want compensation?” A woman in a red jacket calmly rebuked them: “That is an expression that insults human beings. Every person has dignity, and that is why their honor must also be restored.” Throughout the debate, she maintained her composure, elegantly dismantling the right-wing commentators’ distorted arguments point by point. The footage, still widely discussed today, has amassed 10 million views across YouTube and other social media platforms. The woman in the debate was Shin Sugok, a third-generation Zainichi — an ethnically Korean resident of Japan. At the time, she was an entrepreneur running a corporate consulting firm, as well as an author, critic and lecturer. She had achieved an unusually high level of success for a Zainichi woman. Despite countless threats from far-right groups in Japan, she has continued her activism for decades. A documentary film titled “Horoomon,” which chronicles Shin's life

item.title: The Rule of Law Project: New Effort Launched to Probe Corruption & State Violence in U.S.
item.description:
As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, party leaders say they intend to hold Trump officials accountable with stepped-up hearings and investigations. The administration, however, has responded with threats to launch its own investigations into lawmakers for carrying out their oversight responsibilities.

“The oversight function of Congress is well established by the founders. It’s a normal part of government. The separation of powers requires oversight,” says Brad Adams, co-founder of The Rule of Law Project, which seeks to provide outside accountability due to what he describes as the administration’s refusal to investigate “obvious cases of corruption.”

item.title: "It's Just Barbarism": Dr. Feroze Sidhwa Mourns Friend Killed in Israeli Hospital Strike in Gaza
item.description:
Israel’s latest bombing of Nasser Hospital in Gaza on Thursday killed six Palestinians, including surgeon Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira. He was featured in the recent documentary American Doctor, which follows international medical volunteers in Gaza’s battered hospitals as they work alongside Palestinian colleagues.

Israel claimed, without providing evidence, that it targeted a senior Hamas militant in the hospital strike. Israel has repeatedly bombed medical facilities in Gaza since the start of the genocide in October 2023, even though such attacks are prohibited under international law.

“It’s just barbarism. I don’t know why we’re supporting this,” says Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, one of the titular American doctors in the documentary, who demands accountability for Israel’s actions and a change in U.S. policy toward the country. “That’s an American-made bomb dropped by an American-made airplane burning American-supplied jet fuel.”

Sidhwa also comments on the catastrophic flooding in Gaza that has swamped the temporary shelters of tens of thousands of displaced Palestinians as Israel continues to block the entry of shelter materials into the territory. As a result, “babies are going to die of hypothermia in Gaza for the fourth year in a row,” Sidhwa says.

item.title: "Parasitic Technology": Could Jensen Huang/Nvidia Scandal Prompt Rethink About AI?
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with an employee and a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials accuse of spying for Beijing. The company says Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the board searches for a permanent replacement.

Nvidia’s computer chips are at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, driving the company’s value above $4 trillion and making Huang one of the most influential business leaders in the world. His spectacular fall from the company he co-founded in 1993 comes as the U.S. stock market has become highly dependent on a handful of AI-related companies and amid intense competition between the United States and China over control of the technology, with access to Nvidia’s chips becoming a major point of contention between the two countries.

Tech critic Paris Marx notes that the AI industry’s “circular financing,” in which companies are both clients and investors for one another, has created systemic risk.

We also speak with Ramesh Srinivasan, director of the AI Futures Lab at UCLA, who says the “soap opera” of the Huang scandal has exposed “how precarious the governance of this AI truly is,” with only a handful of people and firms controlling “incredibly powerful technology that feeds off of all of us and the planet.”
item.source:markdown:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with an employee and a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials accuse of spying for Beijing. The company says Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the board searches for a permanent replacement.
Nvidia’s computer chips are at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, driving the company’s value above $4 trillion and making Huang one of the most influential business leaders in the world. His spectacular fall from the company he co-founded in 1993 comes as the U.S. stock market has become highly dependent on a handful of AI-related companies and amid intense competition between the United States and China over control of the technology, with access to Nvidia’s chips becoming a major point of contention between the two countries.
Tech critic Paris Marx notes that the AI industry’s “circular financing,” in which companies are both clients and investors for one another, has created systemic risk.
We also speak with Ramesh Srinivasan, director of the AI Futures Lab at UCLA, who says the “soap opera” of the Huang scandal has exposed “how precarious the governance of this AI truly is,” with only a handful of people and firms controlling “incredibly powerful technology that feeds off of all of us and the planet.”

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to step down in big blow to AI boom
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the artificial intelligence (AI) industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday. It named former Synopysys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 percent, will exit the board as well. Nvidia shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market. Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. Huang's exit plunges the $4 trillion

item.title: Preorders open for Samsung, Google, Gentle Monster smart glasses
item.description: Samsung Electronics and Google unveiled the full lineup of smart glasses created in collaboration with eyewear brands Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, opening preorders for 30 models Thursday. Dubbed Intelligent Eyewear, the glasses are powered by Google's Gemini AI, allowing users to explore their surroundings, access information through real-time conversations and interact more intuitively in everyday situations. The glasses are compatible with both Samsung Galaxy smartphones and Apple iPhones. According to Google, users can summon Gemini through a simple voice command or by touching the glasses' frames to check their Google Calendar schedules or add items they are looking at to their shopping lists. Google Translate also provides real-time voice translation in more than 70 languages, helping users understand signs written in foreign languages, while Gemini's Guided Vision feature offers conversational audio descriptions to assist blind and low-vision users, as well as those who need additional visual guidance in everyday situations. Google and Samsung each offered glimpses to four mod

item.title: Scandal-hit Jensen Huang loses his shine in his birthplace Taiwan
item.description: TAIPEI — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been widely adored like a rock star in his birthplace, Taiwan. That image is now tainted after the FBI began an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese agent. Like the rest of the world, the island was shocked by the scandal over Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman reportedly described as a Chinese spy by U.S. officials. A video of the pair visiting a restaurant in the capital city of Taipei in 2025 went viral and was broadcast globally. The 63-year-old poster boy for the artificial intelligence revolution was born in Taiwan and spent his early years there before he moved to the United States for his schooling. He regularly visits Taiwan for business events. Jane Hsieh’s tofu pudding shop was one of many restaurants and stores in Taipei that proudly displayed photos of Jensen Huang visiting their premises. Hsieh, 70, was first shocked by the dramatic headlines and felt deep regret for him, saying Huang used to have a near-perfect public image. item.title: N. Korean FM slams G7 nations' call for denuclearization, says its nuclear pursuit remains 'steadfast'
item.description: North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui denounced Thursday a joint call from major countries for denuclearization of the regime, saying its commitment to nuclear buildup remains "steadfast." Choe made the remarks in a commentary released by state media, after the Group of Seven (G7) advanced nations issued a joint statement following their foreign ministers' meeting in Paris earlier this week. The joint statement strongly condemned the North's illicit nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs, reaffirming their commitment to realizing the "complete denuclearization" of North Korea in accordance with U.N. Security Council (UNSC) resolutions. The UNSC resolutions ban Pyongyang from developing those weapons. "I strongly condemn and reject the G7's vicious criticism about our state's constitutional right and reaffirm the DPRK's steadfast will for nuclear possession in the clearest terms," Choe said in the commentary, carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). item.title: Kim Yoon-seok, Koo Kyo-hwan deliver gripping tension in snowy thriller 'White Blast'
item.description: Actors Kim Yoon-seok and Koo Kyo-hwan reunite on screen for the first time in five years in "White Blast," delivering a sharp, intense mystery thriller where psychological tension and dark humor collide inside a snowbound rural train station. Directed by Hong Eui-jeong and Park Sun-woo, the upcoming movie is considered one of the most anticipated Korean releases this winter. With a compact 89-minute runtime, the movie relies heavily on the dynamic between its two lead actors. Set against the heavy snowfall in mountainous Gangwon Province, the story follows Gap-soo (Kim), a veteran stationmaster just one day away from retirement, and Hyeon-taek (Koo), his newly assigned successor. When a mysterious corpse turns up at the isolated station during a severe snowstorm, the two men are drawn into a tense psychological battle. Because the two actors carry the majority of the story, their shifting emotional states drive the film’s dense atmosphere, even creating moments of unexpected humor amid the freezing cold. Director Hong, who gained acclaim for her 2020 film "Voice of Silence," explained

item.title: Seoul vows continued Ukraine aid despite POW row
item.description: South Korea's foreign ministry said Thursday it would maintain its commitment to supporting Ukraine despite a diplomatic dispute over Kyiv's transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul. "As a responsible member of the international community, we will continue to maintain our principled position on providing assistance to Ukraine," a foreign ministry official told AFP. The JoongAng Ilbo newspaper reported this week that the foreign ministry requested around $100 million in aid for Ukraine in next year's budget, including $50 million for a NATO trust fund and $20 million in humanitarian assistance. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said in July that the country had pledged $100 million in comprehensive assistance to Ukraine at a NATO summit. "Our government will continue to provide humanitarian assistance needed by the Ukrainian people while also taking part in international efforts to support Ukraine's recovery and reconstruction," Lee said at the time. The foreign ministry official's comment followed tensions between the two countries sparked by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zel

item.title: Megaspeed, firm central to Jensen Huang's scandal, pledges to cooperate with US probe
item.description: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered data center company at the center of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s scandal, pledged Thursday to cooperate with investigations into potential risks to U.S. national security. In its first statement since Huang admitted to having an affair with a Chinese woman and former executive of the company, Megaspeed International said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan. Nvidia's board of directors was reported to be meeting to discuss Huang's situation, but there was no word early Thursday on any outcome from those discussions. The company has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Details about Huang’s affair with the woman are unclear. The New York Times reported

item.title: Cheonghae unit to come under on-scene commander's tactical control in limited manner: Seoul
item.description: South Korea's key anti-piracy unit will come under an on-scene commander's tactical control during a multinational security mission under a motion to expand its operational scope, but such authority will be exercised in a "very restricted" manner, Seoul officials said Thursday. The defense ministry submitted to the National Assembly this week a revised motion to expand the operational scope of the Cheonghae Unit from the current zone in waters off the Somali coast to south of Oman in the Arabian Sea, about 650 kilometers away from the Strait of Hormuz. The motion stipulates that the unit will be placed under the "tactical control" of an on-scene commander when it engages in multinational maritime security missions, led by the U.S.-led Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) or the European Union. Tactical control refers to limited authority exercised for the application of military force or tactical use of combat support assets within the assigned mission or task. item.title: N. Korea warns of action against US-led naval buildup
item.description: North Korea on Thursday denounced what it called a U.S.-led naval buildup and nuclear submarine programs, warning it would counter the growing naval threat with unspecified "action." Kim Jong-sik, first vice department director of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, made the remarks in a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). "Arms build-up of the U.S. and its vassal allies for seizing a maritime edge in the Asia-Pacific region has emerged as a new dangerous factor seriously disturbing regional peace and security," Kim said. He described nuclear submarine programs in South Korea, Japan and Australia as the "detailed implementation" of a new U.S. security strategy aimed at "securing the maritime hegemony." "This has become a root cause of seriously undermining the strategic balance in the region and sparking off a new arms race," he claimed. The enemies' naval buildup and the threat it poses to its security are "a very grave challenge," he said, and the North's response "will not be merely confined to denouncing it." Kim Jong-sik, first vice department director of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, made the remarks in a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). "Arms build-up of the U.S. and its vassal allies for seizing a maritime edge in the Asia-Pacific region has emerged as a new dangerous factor seriously disturbing regional peace and security," Kim said. He described nuclear submarine programs in South Korea, Japan and Australia as the "detailed implementation" of a new U.S. security strategy aimed at "securing the maritime hegemony." "This has become a root cause of seriously undermining the strategic balance in the region and sparking off a new arms race," he claimed. The enemies' naval buildup and the threat it poses to its security are "a very grave challenge," he said, and the North's response "will not be merely confined to denouncing it." item.title: Foreign correspondents' club in Seoul voices concern over Russia's detention of Japanese journalist
item.description: A foreign correspondents' club based in Seoul on Thursday expressed deep concern over Russia's detention of a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage, stressing that legitimate journalistic activities must be respected. Last month, Russia's Federal Security Service said it had detained a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper in the far eastern Sakhalin region on suspicion of espionage. "Gathering information in the public interest is fundamental to journalism. Legitimate newsgathering and reporting activities must be respected, and any action that threatens a journalist's personal safety on such grounds cannot be justified," the Seoul Foreign Correspondents' Club (SFCC) board said in a statement posted on its website. It also called on Russian authorities to "ensure the physical safety and legal rights of the detained journalist and clearly state the reasons for the detention." The journalist was later transferred to Moscow, where a court ordered him held in pretrial detention, according to foreign media reports.

item.description: K-pop boy group ATEEZ, already a major force on the global music scene, is enjoying a new level of recognition at home following the success of its hit song "BAD" — with members saying even everyday encounters have changed, from receiving extra freebies at shops to being recognized without having to introduce themselves. The album marks ATEEZ's first comeback since "BAD" became a sensation, helping the group expand its popularity among the general public in Korea after years of building a strong international fan base. item.title: Korean won hits 15-day high against US dollar on foreign inflows
item.description: The Korean won extended gains to its strongest level in 15 days against the U.S. dollar Thursday, as foreign investors remained net buyers of local stocks. The won was quoted at 1,330.7 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 2.9 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in afternoon trading, the won rose to a high of 1,327.7 won per dollar, marking the strongest level since Oct. 28. The won's advance was also supported by local exporters' dollar sales. Foreign investors bought a net 340 billion won ($255 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, while the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index dipped 0.61 percent to close at 5,342.73.

item.title: KEPCO Q3 net plunges 78% on higher fuel costs
item.description: The state-run Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) said Thursday its third-quarter net profit plunged 78 percent from a year earlier due to higher fuel costs. Net profit for the three months ended in September fell to 835.89 billion won from 3.79 trillion won in the same period last year, the company said in a press release. "Electricity sales declined, while global thermal coal prices continued to rise in the third quarter, weighing on our bottom line, among other factors," a company spokesperson said. Combined fuel costs for KEPCO's power-generating subsidiaries, including Korea South-East Power, exceeded 2.2 trillion won in the third quarter, weighing on earnings, the company said. Operating profit plunged 70.9 percent to 1.64 trillion won from 5.65 trillion won during the same period, while sales fell 2.6 percent to 26.85 trillion won from 27.57 trillion won. KEPCO said it would closely monitor volatile energy prices while maintaining an emergency management system focused on improving its financial position through cost reductions and profitability-driven operations. item.title: Lee says Korean capital market undervalued, urges measures to boost competitiveness
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung said Thursday that Korea's capital market remains undervalued, calling for measures to boost its global competitiveness and attract long-term investments. The president made the remarks at a meeting with his key aides at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, as Korea's stock market has experienced significant volatility in recent months. After reaching an all-time closing high of 9,114.55 points in late June, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) closed at 5,342.73 points on Thursday, leaving many investors on edge. The president said the country's capital market has been significantly affected by recent external uncertainties. Given the country's economic fundamentals and corporate competitiveness, Korea's capital market "is an attractive investment destination that still remains undervalued," Lee told the meeting. He said government efforts should be focused on creating an environment in which the capital market receives its fair valuation, allowing its sound development to translate into increased household wealth and improved livelihoods for the public. item.title: Korea, Belgium discuss leak of personal data of President Lee, Europe trip entourage
item.description: Korea and Belgium have discussed the leak of personal information belonging to President Lee Jae Myung and members of his entourage during his June trip to Belgium and other parts of Europe, and agreed to maintain close communication on the matter, Seoul's foreign ministry said Thursday. The issue was discussed during a Seoul meeting between First Vice Foreign Minister Park Yoon-joo and Theodora Gentzis, secretary-general of Belgium's foreign ministry, held Friday, according to the ministry. "During the meeting, ways to promote cooperation in various areas were discussed, and the data leak was also discussed," ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon told a press briefing in response to a reporter's question about possible cooperation between the two countries on the incident. "We take this matter seriously and are conducting an investigation. The two sides agreed to continue communicating closely," Park added. The leak came to light after a file containing personal information of 168 people aboard the presidential aircraft, including Lee and first lady Kim Hea Kyung, was uploaded to VirusTot

item.title: [COVER STORY] Korean investors in Nvidia suffer estimated $2.4 bil. in valuation losses
item.description: A deepening scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is unnerving Korean investors, as the chip giant's shares are falling and uncertainty mounts over his future. Nvidia is the second-most-held U.S. stock among Korean investors after Tesla, leaving local shareholders exposed to mounting losses as the chipmaker's shares plunged amid the scandal. Korean investors held about $13.65 billion worth of Nvidia shares as of Thursday, according to data from the Korea Securities Depository. An estimated 800,000 retail investors in Korea own shares in the chipmaker. Nvidia shares have fallen nearly 15 percent since the company announced an investigation into these allegations. Assuming the retail investors maintained their holdings, the 15 percent decline in shares would amount to an estimated $2.4 billion in valuation losses. The losses extend beyond direct shareholdings. Some 153 exchange-traded funds (ETFs) listed on the Korea Exchange have exposure to Nvidia. The ACE Nvidia Bond Mixed ETF, with assets of about 197.9 billion won ($148 million), has roughly 30 percent of its portfolio invested in N

item.description: Actor Yeo Jin-goo has made a rare public appearance nearly 11 months after enlisting in the military, drawing attention with his noticeably more muscular physique. On Wednesday, photos of Yeo during his military service surfaced on online communities after U.S. Judge Kirsten Brunson shared them on LinkedIn. Brunson said she attended the 26th Korean Military English Speaking Competition as a judge at Camp Humphreys, a major U.S. military installation in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province. item.title: Korean retail investors struggle to cut losses, holding on to or buying more losing stocks
item.description: Two-thirds of Korean retail investors hold on to losing stocks or buy more in an attempt to lower their average purchase price, rather than sell at a loss, a report showed Thursday. The findings are based on an online survey of 1,000 people in their 20s to 50s with experience investing in domestic or overseas stocks, conducted by financial research institute Toss Insight from July 11 to Aug. 21. Of the respondents, 42.2 percent said they continued holding losing stocks, while another 24.4 percent said they bought more shares to bring down their average purchase price. The survey also found that investors who cut their losses according to predetermined rules were less likely to report losses in stocks. Over the previous year, the share reporting losses stood at 26.5 percent in this group, compared with 41.7 percent among those who continued holding losing stocks. It also revealed a gap between investors’ perceived risk tolerance and their actual exposure. item.title: Once a cheap meal, gimbap sees steepest price hike in Seoul
item.description: Gimbap, long considered an affordable meal in Korea, has seen the steepest price increase among popular dining options in Seoul this year, with the average price of a roll approaching 4,000 won ($2.80), up more than 5 percent from the end of last year. According to data released Wednesday by the Korea Consumer Agency's price information portal, Champrice, the average price of a roll of gimbap in Seoul reached 3,923 won in September, up 5.4 percent from 3,723 won in December last year. This was the largest increase among eight popular dining options tracked in Seoul: naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles), bibimbap (rice mixed with vegetables), kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), jjajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce), samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), kalguksu (hand-cut noodles) and gimbap. At many gimbap chains, even a basic roll already costs more than 4,000 won. Prices vary by location, but a roll typically costs more than 5,000 won at well-known franchises like Gimgane and more than 4,000 won at Kobongmin and Teacher Kim. Bibimbap recorded the second-larg

item.title: Police seek arrest warrant for father in killing of son's alleged rape victim
item.description: Police sought an arrest warrant Thursday for a 59-year-old man, surnamed Jin, suspected of killing a 15-year-old girl who was the alleged victim in a statutory rape case involving his son, as investigators continued efforts to establish the motive. The Seongbuk Police Station in Seoul requested the warrant on suspicion of murder. Jin was taken into emergency custody at around 1:40 a.m. Wednesday after allegedly stabbing the girl to death at a shared accommodation property in Seongbuk District, northern Seoul. It remains unclear what motivated him to kill her. Police will bring in a criminal profiler to help determine his motive and seek forensic analysis from the National Forensic Service. His son, 20, has been under investigation on suspicion of statutory rape involving the victim in January. Under Korean law, sexual intercourse between a person aged 19 or older and a minor aged 13 to 15 constitutes statutory rape, regardless of whether the minor consented. item.title: Naver clinches $1.5 bil. AI computing deal with US firm
item.description: Naver has signed a 2 trillion-won ($1.5 billion) computing services supply contract with a U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) inference company, securing an initial customer for its AI infrastructure business ahead of the commercial launch planned in the first half of next year. “This is a meaningful contract that confirms actual market demand and the initial commercial viability of the AI factory business,” CEO Choi Soo-yeon said during the company's third-quarter earnings call Thursday. "Revenue is also expected to be generated sequentially as commercial services begin in the first half of next year." AI factory is Nvidia's term referring to next-generation data centers generating tokens. The contract covers computing services involving next-generation graphics processing units (GPUs), with the initial supply scheduled for 2027. Naver is developing its AI factory business in partnership with the Canadian asset manager Brookfield and U.S. chipmaker Nvidia. item.title: [EXPLAINER] Why Korea's mandatory tender offer plan is drawing global scrutiny
item.description: The proposed revival of Korea's mandatory tender offer system, abolished in 1998 following the Asian financial crisis, has reignited debate nearly three decades later. The idea behind the system is simple: When someone buys a company, smaller shareholders should have a chance to sell their shares at the same price as the company's largest shareholder. Under the bill pending in the National Assembly, a buyer taking control of a company would have to purchase enough shares through a public tender offer to raise its ownership to at least 50 percent plus one share. The goal is to protect minority shareholders, particularly retail investors, who could otherwise miss out on the higher prices paid in corporate takeovers. Here's why the rule matters: Imagine Company A wants to take over Company B. Company B's largest shareholder, Kim, owns 40 percent of its shares, while smaller shareholders own the remaining 60 percent. item.title: KakaoBank simplifies banking for foreign residents with mobile account service
item.description: KakaoBank’s account service for foreign residents attracted 20,000 accounts in its first month, drawing customers from 124 countries, the bank said Thursday. Introduced in October, the account is available to foreign residents aged 19 and older and can be opened through the bank’s app in about five minutes. Customers can also apply for debit cards and send money overseas through the app without visiting a branch. The bank streamlines registration through the government’s Public MyData service, which retrieves personal details such as names, nationalities, addresses and occupations. The service allows users to access their administrative records held by public institutions or request that those records be shared with third parties. Applicants can also submit required documents, including employment certificates and pay statements, directly through the app. Myanmar nationals accounted for the largest share of account holders at 30.3 percent, followed by Chinese nationals at 18 percent, Vietnamese at 16.6 percent, Thai at 4.8 percent and Japanese at 4.6 percent. item.title: Korea Zinc loses court battle over curbs on Young Poong's voting rights
item.description: A court ruled Thursday that a resolution passed at Korea Zinc's annual shareholder meeting last year that restricted the voting rights of Young Poong Corp. and private equity firm MBK Partners Ltd. must be nullified. Young Poong and MBK formed an alliance under an agreement signed in September 2024 to secure management control of Korea Zinc, the world's largest refined zinc smelter. Since then, the two parties have jointly exercised their voting rights, prompting Korea Zinc Chairman Choi Yun-beom to wage a protracted battle to fend off their takeover bid. The Seoul Central District Court ordered Korea Zinc to revoke the resolution adopted at its March 2025 shareholder meeting in a lawsuit filed by the Young Poong-MBK alliance. The court said that Korea Zinc cannot restrict the voting rights of existing shareholders by invoking rules governing cross-shareholdings as a means of defending its management control. item.title: Seoul shares snap 2-day rally amid escalating Nvidia risks
item.description: Korean stocks fell 0.6 percent Thursday to end their two-day rally, weighed heavily down by Nvidia's leadership risks. The local currency was trading higher against the U.S. dollar. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) closed down 32.63 points, or 0.61 percent, at 5,342.73, reversing from a 4.39 percent rise on Tuesday and a 2.6 percent gain on Wednesday. After opening 0.2 percent higher, the index fluctuated between gains and losses throughout the morning trading session, rising as high as 5,458.84. U.S. media said Nvidia's board was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang following reports on Huang's alleged multiple extramarital affairs. Investor sentiment was largely affected by Huang's future as the U.S. chip giant is in close business ties with Korean tech companies. Trade volume was light at 233.7 million shares worth 20.6 trillion won ($15.5 billion), with losers outnumbering winners 595 to 268. item.description: Major tech-intensive firms here are stepping up internal security training and vigilance against industrial espionage, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made headlines for his reported affair with Alice Huang, who is suspected of being linked to Chinese intelligence. The allegations have heightened concerns among technology companies that personal relationships and social interactions could be exploited to compromise sensitive corporate information. Major U.S. technology companies, including OpenAI, have also been strengthening counterintelligence training for employees. Some companies have reportedly advised workers to take precautions in their daily lives, including avoiding wearing clothing with company logos outside the workplace. The heightened vigilance is also spreading among Korean semiconductor companies, which handle highly sensitive technologies and intellectual property. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have been strengthening security education for employees, as the importance of advanced semiconductor technologies grows. item.title: Special counsel raids NEC over fabricated document on security check
item.description: Investigators raided the National Election Commission (NEC) on Thursday over suspicions the election watchdog falsified an official document to exaggerate the security of its computer servers, a special counsel team said. Twenty-five personnel, including two prosecutors, were sent to the NEC headquarters in Gwacheon, just south of Seoul, and two contractors to execute a search and seizure warrant on related charges, according to the team led by independent counsel Lee Tae-han. The allegation dates back to 2023, when a joint security check involving the National Intelligence Service (NIS) and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) found the NEC had exaggerated the results of its own security inspection amid concerns over the vulnerability of its computer servers to cyberattacks. The NEC had reported a perfect score of 100 the previous year, but a reassessment by the NIS and KISA produced a score of only 31.5. item.title: Chances of Trump-Kim meeting at APEC grow slim
item.description: A summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un appears unlikely at next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering in Shenzhen, China, a Cheong Wa Dae official and security analysts said Thursday, despite Trump’s earlier talk of a potential meeting. The assessment comes as the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections have weakened Trump’s momentum for unconventional diplomatic initiatives such as a meeting with Kim. item.title: Ministry defends revision of military academy plan as efforts to increase public's acceptance
item.description: The defense ministry said Thursday that a proposed revision to its original plan to merge the Army, Air Force and Navy academies into a unified institution is part of a process to increase public acceptance of the plan and its "completeness." The ministry recently briefed the National Assembly on the revised plan that calls for creating a joint military academy in the central city of Daejeon while retaining the academies of the Navy and Air Force in the southern county of Jinhae and the central city of Cheongju, respectively, and relocating the Army academy to the central Chungcheong region. It initially sought to consolidate the three academies into a unified school to strengthen inter-service cooperation and improve the efficiency of cadet education — a plan that drew opposition from academy alumni, opposition lawmakers, and residents of Jinhae and Cheongju. item.title: Can tougher reappointment rules curb power of Korea's bank holding company chiefs?
item.description: A corporate governance reform package unveiled by the government to boost transparency of CEO succession at financial companies and rein in long-serving chairmen is facing questions over whether it can deliver meaningful change, according to experts Thursday. Their skepticism centers on whether tougher voting requirements will make a difference when incumbent chairmen already enjoy overwhelming shareholder support, and whether independent directors will be able to challenge management in practice. The announcement comes nearly a year after President Lee Jae Myung publicly criticized what he called a “corrupt inner circle” in which a small group of executives takes turns retaining control of financial firms. A central aim of the reform is to curb incumbent CEOs’ influence over the selection of their successors. Under the proposed rules, committees responsible for nominating CEO candidates would consist entirely of independent directors. item.title: Pay rises, tax bites: Korean workers call for income tax reform
item.description: For Lee, a 43-year-old employee at an IT company in Seoul’s Geumcheon District, a bigger paycheck each year has brought little sense of greater financial security. A pay raise initially feels rewarding, he said. But that feeling fades when he checks his pay statement. Taxes and social insurance contributions have also risen, leaving him with less additional take-home pay than expected. “My salary goes up every year, but things still feel tight after paying loan interest, living expenses and my child’s education costs,” Lee said. “A pay raise that merely keeps pace with inflation doesn’t mean we’re better off. Tax thresholds should also reflect rising prices.” His frustration reflects growing calls to overhaul Korea’s income tax system as nominal wage increases fail to deliver greater purchasing power. Korea has eight income tax brackets, with rates ranging from 6 percent to 45 percent on taxable income after deductions. item.title: City-backed startup summit bolsters Seoul's drive to be global innovation hub
item.description: Seoul’s annual startup summit, Try Everything 2026, generated more than 2,000 investment reviews and doubled face-to-face investor meetings, bolstering the city’s ambitions to rank among the world's top startup hubs. The two-day global startup festival, held Sept. 9-10 at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), attracted 8,025 participants, including 1,457 visitors from 67 countries, and featured 912 startups, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday. The number of participants increased 3.8 percent from 7,729 last year, while startup participation rose 4.2 percent from 875 companies. The event recorded 1,141 one-on-one meetings between startups, investors and major corporations, more than twice the 541 meetings held last year. The amount of potential investment under review reached 202.4 billion won ($140 million), up approximately 12 percent from 2025. Organizers expanded dedicated meeting booths from 15 to 40 and strengthened advance matchmaking to encourage substantive discussions and business partnerships. item.title: Korea welcomes record 20 mil. foreign visitors as K-culture fuels tourism boom
item.description: Korea has crossed a milestone that once seemed distant, welcoming more than 20 million foreign tourists in a single year for the first time as the global popularity of Korean culture fuels demand for travel to the country. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism announced that international arrivals surpassed the 20 million mark on Thursday, just 14 years after Korea first recorded 10 million annual visitors in 2012. The achievement marks a new high for the country's tourism industry, with arrivals expected to continue setting records through the end of the year. The surge has also translated into higher spending and more visitors entering through regional gateways, extending tourism's economic benefits beyond the capital. Foreign tourists spent 15.9 trillion won on tourism-related activities through September, up 47.7 percent from the same period last year, according to the ministry. Arrivals through airports outside the Seoul metropolitan area reached 3.24 million, up 37.4 percent, while arrivals through regional seaports totaled 1.58 million, an increase of 14.5 percent. item.title: FM Cho to visit China this week for talks with Wang Yi on N. Korea, bilateral ties
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun will visit China this week for talks with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on North Korea-related issues and bilateral relations, Seoul's foreign ministry said Thursday. Cho is scheduled to make a two-day visit to Beijing starting Friday, during which he will hold talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang and attend a dinner on the same day, according to the ministry. "The two ministers plan to hold wide-ranging discussions on issues of mutual interest, including bilateral relations, developments on the Korean Peninsula and other regional issues," ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon said at a press briefing. Cho's visit follows an invitation from Wang during their talks in Seoul in August. At the time, the two ministers exchanged views on bilateral relations and Korean Peninsula issues, with Cho calling for Beijing to play a constructive role in bringing North Korea back to dialogue. item.title: After dark, Seoul's museums and cultural sites see attendance surge
item.description: Seoul’s museums, historic sites and cultural venues are drawing more visitors after dark, with attendance more than doubling since the city expanded evening opening hours for many popular spots in September. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday that six major cultural attractions recorded approximately 1.198 million visitors from Sept. 15 to Oct. 31, up 110 percent from 569,000 from Aug. 1 to Sept. 14. The increase followed an expansion of evening hours that allows select venues to remain open until 9 p.m. five days a week, giving residents and tourists more opportunities to explore the city after work. More than 85,000 people visited the six venues between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. during the initial period, according to the city. The participating attractions are Seoul Museum of History, Seoul Museum of Craft Art, Seoul Baekje Museum, Unhyeon Palace, Namsangol Hanok Village and the Story of Sejong and Story of Admiral Yi Sunshin exhibition halls at Gwanghwamun. item.title: Singapore Art Week to mark 15 years by taking art to streets
item.description: SINGAPORE — For 11 days next January, art in Singapore will spill out of its museums and galleries. It will light up the facade of a skyscraper in the financial district, fill the historic Padang green, ride a bus through residential neighborhoods and greet commuters at 10 subway stations. That citywide takeover sits at the heart of Singapore Art Week (SAW) 2027, which will mark its 15th edition from Jan. 21 to 31. With Singapore expected to take on the chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in a year that also marks the bloc’s 60th anniversary, this edition will put Southeast Asian art and its creative ties across the region front and center. SAW is organized by the National Arts Council (NAC), a statutory board under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth that champions the arts in Singapore, with support from the Singapore Tourism Board. Launched in 2013 with just over 50 events, the annual season has since grown into the country’s most prominent visual arts event, now spanning more than 100 programs across museums, galleries, independent art

item.title: FTC approves combination of Jin Air, Air Seoul, Air Busan
item.description: The proposed merger of Jin Air, Air Busan and Air Seoul has cleared its final regulatory hurdle, paving the way for the three low-cost carriers (LCCs) to officially operate as a single carrier under the Jin Air brand beginning March 17, the nation’s antitrust authority said Thursday. Under the approvals by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the Fair Trade Commission (FTC), the three carriers will be integrated through Jin Air's absorption of Air Busan and Air Seoul following Korean Air’s acquisition of Asiana Airlines. The approvals remove the major regulatory obstacles to the restructuring of Hanjin Group's airline business, following the planned launch of the integrated Korean Air as a full-service carrier on Dec. 17. Jin Air will assume the assets, liabilities, employees and legal status of the two other carriers. The combined airline will become Korea's largest LCC by fleet size, with about 58 aircraft in operation by the three carriers combined as of the end of 2025. item.title: Grand Korea Leisure earns top ESG rating for 3rd straight year
item.description: Grand Korea Leisure, the state-run operator of Seven Luck foreigner-only casinos, has earned an A rating for the third consecutive year in an annual evaluation of corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices. The state-run casino operator, which runs the Seven Luck brand for foreign visitors, said Thursday it received an overall A grade in the 2026 ESG assessment announced Wednesday by the Korea Institute of Corporate Governance and Sustainability. The company also received A grades in all three individual categories: environmental protection, social responsibility and corporate governance. The annual assessment, conducted by the Korea Institute of Corporate Governance and Sustainability since 2011, evaluates listed companies on their sustainability management practices, with 1,022 companies included in this year's review. item.title: European film festival brings record 23 countries to Seoul
item.description: Seoul is preparing for an unusually wide-ranging cinematic journey through Europe, with films from a record 23 countries set to take over Seoul Museum of History for this year's European Film Festival. The 12th edition of the festival, organized by Seoul Museum of History in partnership with EUNIC Korea and the Delegation of the European Union to the Republic of Korea, will run from Nov. 20 to Dec. 6, with 23 films screened free of charge. This year's theme, "Memories of Past, Visions of Future," explores history, identity, migration, generations, gender and human rights through stories from across Europe. The participating countries include Poland, Italy, Sweden, Spain, Britain, Germany, France, Hungary, Ireland and 14 others, marking the largest international lineup in the festival's history. Screenings will take place at Yajugae Hall inside the museum on nine Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, with evening sessions added to make the program more accessible to workers and students. item.title: Seoul serves up steamed rice as next big tourist attraction
item.description: A bowl of steamed rice, an everyday staple in Korea, could become an unexpected draw for international tourists as Seoul looks to turn its traditional food culture into a new form of culinary tourism. The Seoul Metropolitan Government held a K-Rice Pairing Experience on Wednesday at Seoul Herbal Medicine Center, inviting 12 international students from Korea University to explore the flavors, aromas and textures of Korean rice. The event was part of the city's efforts to develop tourism experiences rooted in local culture and everyday life, moving beyond conventional sightseeing destinations. Participants sampled three Korean rice varieties — Samgwang from Chungcheong Province, Sindongjin from North Jeolla Province and Golden Queen No. 3 from Gyeonggi Province — comparing their textures, aromas and levels of stickiness. They also paired the rice with salted pollock roe, roasted seaweed and kimchi before sampling three traditional alcoholic beverages made from rice.
